column1: # SOURCE-READERS — intentional readers of non-product-source bytes.
# These readers are KEEP rulings: from L1-migration-debt-large-3, and from the
# ticket in each later row's ticket column. They read a runtime fixture, a
# shipped asset, documentation, a committed ledger, or a deliberate parser
# corpus. They do not use a Rust file as the identity of a product item or
# module. A (file, owner) pair may appear here or in MIGRATION-DEBT.tsv, never
# crates/bt-source/tests/tripwire.rs holds the readers of committed documents
# (every committed file that is not .rs) to this list and MIGRATION-DEBT.tsv:
# an item of test or build-support code that includes one, or hands a path
# that reduces to one to any call or method (read_to_string, fs::read,
# File::open, a wrapper such as read_session; judged per call; the mechanism
# column names the callee), with a row on neither is refused
# not see and lists every path it gives up on as a diagnostic).
# The other way round as well: the list is an equality, not an allowlist
# owner) is an item bt-source finds in that file, spelled as the refusal above
# spells a reader, and its `category` column says what holds it:
#   read         the documents the scan finds the item reading are exactly
#                those the subject names (no fewer, no more), and a Rust-source shape written in the item
#   unreduced    the scan's diagnostic names the item: the read exists and the
#                evaluator cannot reduce its path, so its subject is not
#                checked; the row stays while the diagnostic entry does, and
#                when it goes the row is `read` or removed;
#   rust-source  the four Rust-source shapes report every name the subject
#   exception    a reader no scan sees, the blind spot named in its reason.
# No other value, and none missing. The subject is spelled as the mechanism
# resolves it: an include's literal from the row's file's directory, any other
# path from the workspace root; `;` separates several and `*` stands for any
# run inside one segment. A test that reads only a file it writes itself is no
# reader of a committed document and has no row.
